transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um... hi. I guess I'm here because... well, people keep telling me they can't follow what I'm trying to explain. 

At work, mostly. I'm an artist, and... lately, my artist statements and client notes are apparently confusing to people. Even in meetings, they say I just... jump around too much. Like I'll go from talking about the textures, to the budget, and then to... secret meanings, I guess. I don't know. People just say they can't understand me.
Have you always had difficulty explaining your ideas in a way that others can understand, or is this something that's gotten worse over time?

Um... no, not always. It's... just been the last year or so. Maybe a year and two months. That's when I... I switched from community curation to doing independent installation work full-time. So... yeah, since then, I guess.
Do you feel like your thoughts are disjointed or hard to put into words when you're trying to explain something?

I mean... I guess so. Like I was just saying, when I'm writing my statements or talking in those meetings... it just comes out all at once. To me, the textures and the budgets and... the other stuff, it all connects. But when I try to put it into words... yeah. People just say they can't follow it. I don't really know how else to explain it.
Do you ever think that the secret meanings you mention have a special significance that other people don't understand?

I... well. It's just that sometimes things feel... connected. 

Like... if I'm looking at a stain on a canvas, or the way a seam is sewn, or even just... a phrase in an email from a gallery. It feels like... like it's a message. Just for me. Like an instruction, or maybe a warning about what I'm making. 

People tell me it's just a coffee stain or a typo, but... it's really hard to just ignore it. Even when they explain it. It just... it feels important.
Do you ever find yourself able to ignore these feelings of special significance about things like stains or phrases, or do they tend to stick with you?

Um... no, they mostly just stick. I... I get really convinced that they're meant for me. Like an instruction, or a warning about my work. So... even if someone shows me a normal explanation for the stain or the email... it's just very hard for me to let it go.
Do you feel like your thoughts are clear and organized in your own mind, even if you have trouble explaining them to others?

I don't know if "organized" is the right word. Sometimes... they just go really fast. 

Like... I'll be thinking about a piece, and then suddenly there are images, and titles, and... the wording for a grant application... colors... things people said to me. It just all stacks up on top of each other. Before I can even finish thinking about the first thing, the rest is just... there. It's a lot.
Do you feel like these difficulties with explaining your ideas and the special meanings you see in things are causing you a lot of stress or problems in your daily life?

Yes, I suppose so. It's... it's caused some issues. 

I've missed some paid deadlines recently. And... in meetings with collaborators, they get confused by what I'm saying. I had an exhibition that had to be postponed, too. My notes and proposals just... they stopped making enough sense for people to use them. So... yes. It's been stressful.
When you have these thoughts with special meanings, do you feel like they are your own thoughts?
Um... yes. They're my thoughts. I don't... I'm not really sure what you mean by that. They're just in my head, so... yeah, they're mine.
Do you ever feel like these special meanings or instructions are coming from outside your own mind?

Not... exactly outside my mind. But... from things around me, I guess. 

Like... I'll see a certain stain, or the way a seam looks. Or... a specific phrase in an email from a gallery. And I just... I get convinced it's meant specifically for me. Like it's an instruction, or... a warning about my work. 

Sometimes people try to point out a more ordinary explanation for it, but... it's very hard for me to just let it go. It just feels too specific.
Do you believe that these messages or instructions you see in things are specifically intended for you, and not for anyone else?

Yes. Um... like I just said, I get convinced they are meant specifically for me. Nobody else. 

Even if someone else looks at the exact same thing and... and tries to tell me it's just an ordinary email or a normal mark... I can't really let it go. Because it just feels like it's only for me.
Do you ever act on these instructions or warnings that you see in things, like changing your art or making decisions based on them?

Um... I don't think so. I don't really change my art or... do anything big. 

I just... I notice it, mostly. Maybe I'll stop working for a minute, but... I don't really act on it. It just sort of stays in my head.
Have you experienced any significant problems in your relationships with friends or family because of these difficulties with explaining your ideas or the special meanings you see in things?

Um... well, it hasn't really been about friends or family so much. But... it has affected my work. 

I've... I've missed some paid deadlines because of it. And... in meetings with collaborators, they get confused by what I'm saying. My notes and proposals just... they stopped making enough sense for people to use them. 

I even had an exhibition postponed because of it. So... yeah. It causes problems.
Do you ever find yourself changing your daily routines or habits because of these special meanings or instructions you see in things?
Um... no. Not really. I just... I keep doing what I normally do. It doesn't really change my routine or anything.
Do you ever feel like your thoughts are being controlled or influenced by something outside of yourself?
Um... no. I don't think so. They're just... my own thoughts. I don't feel like anything is controlling them.
Have you noticed any problems in your personal relationships, such as with friends or family, because of the way you've been thinking or explaining things lately?
Um... I think you already asked me about that. Like I said before... no, not really. It's mostly just been an issue with my work.
Do you ever feel like you're losing touch with what's real and what's not?
I don't... no. Everything seems normal to me. I know what's going on around me, so... no, I don't feel like that.
Do you think these special meanings or messages could be just your imagination playing tricks on you?

Um... I don't know. It doesn't feel like my imagination. I just... I get really convinced that certain things, like... a stain, or a seam... or specific phrases in gallery emails... I feel like they're meant specifically for me. Like they're instructions, or warnings about my work. And... even if someone shows me a perfectly ordinary explanation for it, it's... it's very hard for me to let go of that.
Do you feel anxious or upset when you're unable to convince others of the special meanings you see in things?
Um... no. I don't really... try to convince anyone else. I mostly just keep it to myself. So... no, not really.
Do you ever feel like these special meanings or instructions influence your decisions or actions in any way?

Um... I guess... sometimes. I mean, if I think I'm supposed to use a certain color, or... or stop working on a piece... I usually do. But... I don't know. It's just my work. I don't really think about it that much.
Do you ever hear voices or sounds that other people can't hear?

Um... sometimes, I guess. When I'm alone in the studio... I'll hear a woman. Just quietly commenting, like... from behind the shelves. Or I'll smell hot metal near something I haven't finished yet. It... it feels completely real to me. But then I check, and... there's nothing there. So... yeah.
